headline: China's chip exports rose 136% in value to US$45 billion in September, driven by higher chip prices while the number of chips shipped barely changed.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: official customs data, with a clear AI-price effect.
importance_line: It affects buyers of memory chips worldwide, who are paying more, and shows China's chip trade growing despite equipment limits; the figures are customs data, not company results.
summary: The South China Morning Post reports, from Chinese customs data released on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026, that China's integrated-circuit exports rose 136% year on year to US$45 billion in September while shipment volume rose only 1%, which reflects a global memory chip shortage and AI-driven price rises. Customs vice-minister Wang Jun linked the growth to worldwide AI computing investment.
notes: SCMP blocked (HTTP 403); figures and Wang Jun quotes read in Sri Lanka Guardian's account of the same customs data.
